actual_tool_job.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Create one high-resolution portrait-card fusion using exactly two inputs. Image1 is the sole authority for clothing, pose, hair, expression, light, and crop. Image2 provides mascot identity and anatomy only. Transform the human anatomy into a smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot head and body. The face must feature green-ringed black eyes and a source-matching mouth. Preserve the actual short grey temple hair and real brow hair. Maintain a smooth upper lip and chin with no prominent separate moustache or beard. Ensure a serious closed mouth expression. The subject wears a dark navy open naval coat over a white or grey shirt collar and a dark necktie. The head is topped with an actual dark navy or black peaked cap featuring a broad gold decorative band and front motif, with a dark visor. No spectacles are present. The rounded chin must immediately meet a raised and broadened existing neckline, creating a very short broad neck transition with minimal throat exposure. Avoid any separate yellow neck shaft, pointed V funnel, pinched collar, neck rolls, floating collar, clipping, or cream belly bib. Preserve the actual source open garment and observed inner collar or neckwear state, ensuring coherent front and rear collar overlap with contact shadows. Retain the complete tilted dark frame and opaque photographic backing in its exact original color. Include the attached lower-right cream note with faint indistinct upper marks and actual overlap. All solid surfaces must remain opaque, with alpha transparency only outside the complete card silhouette. Do not invent any insignia, text, or accessories. Keep fine primary details understated and indistinct where they are not clearly resolved in the source.
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: IMAGE-LEFT three-quarter naval bust, actual dark NAVY/BLACK peaked cap with broad GOLD decorative band/front motif and dark visor. Short GREY temple hair and real brow HAIR, smooth upper lip/chin with no prominent separate moustache/beard, no spectacles. Keep serious CLOSED mouth. Dark NAVY OPEN naval coat/uniform over WHITE/GREY shirt collar and DARK necktie, limited by note. Preserve exact primary head roll/angle/light/crop and actual cap fittings, no hidden shoulder/chest regalia.
Retain exact primary head angle, expression, cap shape, real hair and visible clothing/decoration areas. One compact near-round yellow mascot head with a clearly ROUNDED short chin immediately contacting raised broad collar, no V-shaped lower-face funnel or yellow shaft. Do not copy the human long neck or angular jaw into mascot anatomy; fit the source collar to the compact rounded head. Preserve actual dark solid cloth and photographic backing opacity. Tiny ambiguous features remain understated; no new badge engraving or decorations hidden behind note. Image1 exact original card; Image2 mascot identity/anatomy only.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
